project.title: Initial-state matching and stability diagnostics for a counter-streaming electron-fluid closure
project.summary: Archived PIC and reloaded fluid initial-state controls with conditional loader calculations and an auxiliary continuum calibration for arXiv:2607.07106v1.
project.research_question: How do the archived initial physical moments differ, what does a conditional public loading rule explain, and which causal or sheet-stability conclusions remain untested?

claims.text: The archived initial PIC and fluid velocity moments differ: the full x-averaged moment-current profile has a relative L2 difference of 9.87 percent, and the two lower-sheet central cells differ by about 11.6 percent. Reloaded fluid output corroborates the posted initializers to roundoff.
claims.evidence_summary: Five CRC32/SHA-256 checked t=0 BP snapshots, embedded inputs byte-identical to the posted Lua decks, all 480x640 fluid cells checked, and full 640-row PIC/fluid profile comparisons.
claims.confidence_note: Physical moment current and velocity-covariance pressure; no native deposited-current file is identifiable. Whole-archive MD5, a matched-state rerun and nonlinear causal significance remain unestablished.

claims.text: The inspected public unweighted thermal-momentum loading rule predicts a mean drift below its cold proper-velocity conversion. An unfitted quadratic-shape sensitivity further accounts for the scale of the archived lower-sheet drift reduction.
claims.evidence_summary: Complete posted PIC deck audit, pinned public loader/deposition source, converged Gaussian quadrature and independent Cartesian moment checks; conditional pointwise and shape predictions remain separate.
claims.confidence_note: Conditional on the public loading rule and stated sampling assumptions; the original executable and custom velocity-diagnostic kernel are not identified or certified.

claims.text: A specified homogeneous two-Maxwellian equilibrium stable to collisionless longitudinal electrostatic perturbations has an overstable mode in the stated finite-isotropization fluid closure.
claims.evidence_summary: Explicit rational Penrose bound, linear system, eigenvalue residual, dielectric residual and Gauss-constraint checks.
claims.confidence_note: Separate nonrelativistic continuum benchmark; no claim that this mode occurred in the source reconnection simulation or of general electromagnetic stability.
